chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid said:

I asked him face-to-face about a man who divorced his wife in the presence of two witnesses during a period of purity, then he traveled and testified to her revocation (raj'ah). When he returned, he divorced her again without sexual intercourse. I asked: Is that permissible for him? He said, 'Yes, her divorce has taken effect.'

Because it is not established that he has the right to divorce his wife with any type of divorce, for we hold that he does not have the right to give her another divorce during the waiting period (iddah).
As for if he divorces her with the Sunnah divorce, then that is permissible.
And that which indicates this distinction is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is a second divorce valid during the waiting period if the husband had already revoked the first divorce?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies that a husband may issue a second revocable divorce during the *iddah* period even after having already revoked the first, as the restriction applies to the total number of divorces rather than the specific timing or type. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the distinction between *Talaq al-Sunnah* (revocable) and *Talaq al-Bid'ah* (irrevocable), ensuring the marital bond remains within the permissible scope of three total divorces. The hadith highlights the procedural flexibility granted to husbands while maintaining the sanctity of the waiting period as a window for reconciliation.
